question: After decades of listening for alien radio signals, how much of the possible search space has been covered?
options: About a tenth of the sky
A hot tub out of the oceans
answer: A hot tub out of the oceans. Wright and colleagues added up every search by sky area, frequency, sensitivity and time, and set it against every place and way a signal could hide. What has been examined compares to a hot tub of water against all of Earth's seas. No fish in it says little.
move: Before calling a search empty, ask how much ground it covered.
ask: Where have I given up after looking in only a few places?
trap: Most nearby stars, since the search has run for decades.
reference: Wright, Kanodia & Lubar, How Much SETI Has Been Done? Finding Needles in the n-dimensional Cosmic Haystack, Astronomical Journal, 2018
